description: Couple filing jointly, ages 50 and 49, wages 200,000 plus 80,000 of investment income: MAGI is over 250,000 by less than the investment income, so the tax is on the excess; wages under 250,000, no additional Medicare tax.
worked:
Filing status: married filing jointly.
Taxpayer: born 1975-03-15, age 50 at the end of 2025.
Spouse: born 1976-12-12, age 49 at the end of 2025.
Form 1040: line 1z wages 200,000; line 2b taxable interest 10,000; line 3a qualified dividends 25,000; line 3b ordinary dividends 30,000; line 7a capital gain 40,000 (Schedule D line 16: net long-term 40,000).
Form 1040 line 9 total income = 200,000 + 10,000 + 30,000 + 40,000 = 280,000; line 10 adjustments 0; line 11a/11b adjusted gross income = 280,000.
Line 12e standard deduction = 31,500 (married filing jointly; no line 12d box: nobody 65 or older or blind).
Schedule 1-A Part V: nobody is 65 or older at the end of the year; senior deduction 0.
Line 14 = 31,500 + 0 = 31,500; line 15 taxable income = 280,000 - 31,500 = 248,500.
Qualified Dividends and Capital Gain Tax Worksheet (Form 1040 line 16):
  line 1 = 248,500; line 2 = 25,000; line 3 = 40,000 (Schedule D lines 15 and 16 both 40,000); line 4 = 65,000; line 5 = 248,500 - 65,000 = 183,500
  line 6 = 96,700; line 7 = smaller of 248,500 and 96,700 = 96,700; line 8 = smaller of 183,500 and 96,700 = 96,700; line 9 = 0 taxed at 0%
  line 10 = smaller of 248,500 and 65,000 = 65,000; line 11 = 0; line 12 = 65,000
  line 13 = 600,050; line 14 = smaller of 248,500 and 600,050 = 248,500; line 15 = 183,500 + 0 = 183,500; line 16 = 65,000; line 17 = smaller of 65,000 and 65,000 = 65,000
  line 18 = 15% x 65,000 = 9,750; line 19 = 65,000; line 20 = 65,000 - 65,000 = 0; line 21 = 20% x 0 = 0
  line 22 (tax on line 5): Tax Rate Schedule Y-1 (married filing jointly or qualifying surviving spouse) on 183,500: 10% x 23,850 = 2,385; 12% x (96,950 - 23,850) = 8,772; 22% x (183,500 - 96,950) = 19,041; total 30,198
  line 23 = 9,750 + 0 + 30,198 = 39,948
  line 24 (tax on line 1): Tax Rate Schedule Y-1 (married filing jointly or qualifying surviving spouse) on 248,500: 10% x 23,850 = 2,385; 12% x (96,950 - 23,850) = 8,772; 22% x (206,700 - 96,950) = 24,145; 24% x (248,500 - 206,700) = 10,032; total 45,334
  line 25 = smaller of 39,948 and 45,334 = 39,948 -> Form 1040 line 16 (regular tax)
Form 8960: lines 1 + 2 + 5a = 10,000 interest + 30,000 dividends + 40,000 gain = 80,000 (line 8; no deductions, line 12 = 80,000; pensions, IRA distributions and Social Security are not investment income).
  line 13 MAGI = 280,000; line 14 = 250,000 (married filing jointly); line 15 = 30,000; line 16 = smaller of 80,000 and 30,000 = 30,000 (the MAGI over the threshold is the lesser); line 17 = 3.8% x 30,000 = 1,140
Form 8959 Part I: line 1 Medicare wages (W-2 box 5) = line 4 = 200,000; line 5 = 250,000 (married filing jointly); line 6 = 200,000 - 250,000, zero or less, so 0; line 7 = 0.9% x 0 = 0 (additional Medicare tax).
Total tax = 39,948 regular + 1,140 net investment income tax + 0 additional Medicare tax = 41,088.
